issue_detail.value: `tools/skill-tests.sh`, the unittest runner `npm test` uses, loads no conftest, so the harness-variable scrub BG1197 added never runs there and the meter tests fail under a Cursor session - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator
A Cursor Composer or Grok session in Fast mode is priced at the standard rate, because the model id a reading carries cannot tell Fast from standard - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

`sprint.py lane land` removes the builder's worktree, so the builder cannot be resumed for a repair after a REJECT and a fresh builder must re-read the unit from cold - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

The resume brief has three edges its tests do not pin: a batch listed out of plan order, a `-qa.none` landing marker read as in flight, and a Sprint Goal holding a newline that breaks `parse` - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

Two US1146 persona checks cannot catch a swapped Primary, and `validate.py personas` compares the whole Interface cell, so a card reverted to Primary passes AC2's own Verify - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

`help/sprint.md` still names a lane hand-in `<unit>-claims.json` under the id as typed, which BG1303's landing now keys by the normalised id, and `refine seams` still pairs a schema-3 unit with itself - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

`sprint.py handoff` silently drops an `--agent` naming a unit outside the batch, both new verbs crash on an unreadable run state, and the next-step line's stream is unpinned - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator
A Copilot `credit_usd` of 0 is accepted and prices every Copilot reading at $0, and reference-sprint.md's list of price sources omits the newer ones - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

Five Copilot model ids priced from the shared OpenAI entries stay token-priced under `pricing.copilot_billing: requests`, so a request-billed Copilot run on one of them is billed twice - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator
Trevor Hale's Scenario check misses a capitalised offer and a negation outside its word list, so changelog.d/US1147.md claims more than the AC7 test holds - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator
The commit-msg trailer check still refuses commit 089008d5's `Refs: US1090`, whose only record is a waiver row in decisions.md - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

The commit-msg hook misses git's scissors line under a non-default `core.commentChar`, the multi-id rule still reads trailers below it, and `_ledger_rows` and BG1264's fragment say an edited ledger row owns nothing - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

No test replays a page filed before the Copilot billing basis existed, a mixed run's page drops the 'plan bills by request' reason, and US1145's lane-return test copies the call instead of running it - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

A hand-run mutation pass can leave a stale `.pyc` that Python reuses after the source is restored, so a later test run, the commit hook's among them, judges the mutant rather than the code - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

`sprint.py handoff` writes a resume brief while a lane is still in flight, so the wave boundary reference-sprint.md defines is stated but not enforced, and four files still say no command writes a handoff - not-stop-ship, ruled by orchestrator

A verdict file's `\;` escape, which the review brief prescribes for a semicolon inside a finding, still splits the finding when `critic.py record --from-verdict` reads it, leaving an untagged piece the record refuses

`artifact.py new --type story --epic <a Done epic>` leaves the epic Done, so its parent request derives Complete although the new story is Draft, and `refine apply` refuses to add the deferred slice of an already-decomposed request
